Reference / io/stdin

io/stdin#

The process input, as lines of text or as bytes (#221).

Version: v1.0.0

Synopsis#

for Stdin() -> line { … }                               // UTF-8 lines
let command = Stdin().line();
for Stdin(decoding: InputDecoding.lenient) -> line { … } // bad bytes as U+FFFD
let chunk = Stdin().bytes(limit: 65536);                 // bytes as they come
for Stdin().chunks(size: 65536) -> chunk { … }

Description#

The process input, as lines of text or as bytes (#221).

A line is what comes before LF, without that LF and one CR right before it; a last line without LF counts too. Decoding is strict UTF-8 unless told: InvalidUtf8 then names the first bad byte of the line. line() throws EndOfInput at the end; for stops there. Stdin.bytes(limit) returns at most limit unmodified bytes; limit must be positive and [] is stable EOF.

Every Stdin value reads the same process input through one buffer of the runtime, so lines and bytes may be mixed and Stdin() made anew each time. On a terminal, what was written to Stdout shows before the program waits. The wait blocks: no other task runs until input comes, unlike the asynchronous streams of a child process (Process.streams).

Utf8Input decodes any Reading, a Stdin too:

let input = Utf8Input(origin: Stdin());
let command is string = input.line();
let remainder is string = input.content();
input.close();

Utf8Input buffers bytes read ahead from its non-owned Reading. line() splits on LF, removes that LF and one immediately preceding CR, and preserves every other character. A final non-empty line is returned without requiring a terminator. content() returns all remaining decoded text without newline normalization. Both operations use strict UTF-8 and throw EndOfInput only when upstream EOF is known and the private buffer is empty.

close() is idempotent, clears the decoder buffer and does not close the wrapped Reading. Reading after close throws ClosedInput.

enum InputDecoding#

enum InputDecoding = (strict, lenient)

How input bytes become text: strict UTF-8 refuses a bad byte with InvalidUtf8; lenient puts U+FFFD for each ill-formed sequence, as browsers do.
